# **<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE                                           Date Issued: 20</mark>**<sup>**th**</sup> **<mark>August 2009</mark>** 



## **Copper: Preliminary Data for May 2009** 

The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released preliminary data for May world copper supply and demand in its August 2009 Copper Bulletin.  The Bulletin is available for sale upon request. 

According to the preliminary ICSG data, the refined copper market balance for May 2009 indicated a deficit of around 95,000 metric tonnes (t), principally owing to continued high net Chinese imports of refined copper and the consequent increase in their monthly apparent usage.*  When making seasonal adjustments for world refined production and usage, May showed a deficit of about 65,000 t. The apparent refined copper balance for the first 5 months of 2009, including revisions to data previously presented, indicates a production deficit of 150,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of 60,000 t). This compares with a production deficit of 183,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of 25,000 t) for the same period in 2008. These data correlate well to reported stock changes of 110,000 t and 150,000 t, respectively, over the same comparative periods. 

In the first 5 months of 2009, world usage is estimated to have decreased by 1.1% compared with that in the same period of 2008 as a 44% increase in Chinese apparent usage partially offset a decrease of 18% in the remaining countries.  Chinese apparent usage has increased by almost one million tons in the first 5 months of 2009, compared with the same period of 2008.  Copper usage remained weak in other important markets such as the EU-15 countries, Japan, and the United States, where it decreased by 25%, 40%, and 21%, respectively. These three regions currently represent around 30% of the world total copper usage. 

World mine production grew by 2.2% (135,000 t) in the first 5 months of 2009 compared with that in the same period of 2008, when operational problems led to reduced production: Concentrate production grew by 1% while solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) was up by 7%.  The main contributor to growth was Indonesia, where production increased by 90% (recovering from 2008 operational constraints). Output in other major producers was down (Chile -4.4%, China -12% and the United States -3%).  Capacity utilization rates have increased slowly since March but are still significantly below an average utilization rate of 87% over the past 5 years. 

In the first five months of 2009, world refined production decreased by 0.7% compared with that in the same period of 2008: Primary production was practically unchanged while secondary production (from scrap) decreased by 4.2%, reflecting the global scarcity of scrap.  Announced production cuts led to decreases in refined production of around 9% in the EU-15 countries, 12% in North America, and 3% in Asia (ex-China). Increases of around 11% in Chile and 4% in China were n

ot sufficient to offset decreases in the other regions. Refined production capacity utilization fell to around 77% compared with an average of around 83% over the past 5 years. The average LME cash price for July 2009 was US$5,215.54 per tonne, up from the June 2009 average of US$5,013.95 per tonne. The 2009 high and low copper prices through the end of July were US$5,750.00 and US$3,050.50 per tonne, respectively, and the average was US$4,228.73 per tonne. As of the end July 2009, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 383,116 t, a decrease of 6,567 t from stocks held at the end of December 2008. Compared to the June levels, stocks were down at SHFE and at COMEX but up at the LME.
